 Pakistan Cricket Board declines permission to over-50s team for playing in India
 The Pakistan Cricket Board has denied its over-50s team permission to compete in the International Masters Cricket World Cup in India next January. The champions withdrew despite visa and high-level security assurances from the hosts.
 Advertisement Pakistan cricket image for representation By: Press Trust of India New Delhi , Oct 21, 2026 19:05 IST Last Updated Oct 21, 2026 19:05 IST Published by Akshay Ramesh Oct 21, 2026 19:05 IST The Pakistan Cricket Board has declined a request from the over-50s team to participate in the International Masters Cricket World Cup being hosted by India in January next year.
 Pakistan won the last edition of the tournament held in Sri Lanka last year, but this time the board has informed the Pakistan Veterans Cricket Association that they are not permitted to travel and play in India.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story "We have informed the organisers about our withdrawal from the World Cup so that they can arrange for an alternate team," Fawad Ijaz, who heads the PVCA, said on Wednesday.
 Ijaz said that the organisers and host nation had assured the PVCA of granting its team visas and providing high-level security, after which it had sought permission from the PCB and the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Interior to participate.
 Ijaz revealed that Pakistan's interior minister Mohsin Naqvi, who also heads the PCB, informed them they are not permitted to play in India.
 The Pakistan Hockey Federation had also recently refused to travel to India to play in the Asian Champions Trophy and was replaced by Bangladesh.
 Pakistan and India, due to strained relations, play cricket against each other only in multi-nation events and at neutral venues. - Ends Advertisement Also Watch
